import re, time

with open('/app/regex.txt') as f:
    pattern = f.read().strip()

# Exact usage from task description
log_text = """2024-01-01 10.0.0.1 login ok
192.168.1.100 2024-01-02 12:00:00 request
2024-01-03 2024-01-04 172.16.0.5 two dates
1134-12-1234 10.0.0.1 fake date
2024-02-30 10.0.0.1 bad feb
2024-02-29 10.0.0.1 ok feb
no date here 8.8.8.8
2024-12-31 255.255.255.255 2024-12-31"""

matches = re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE)
print("log test:", matches)
expected = ["2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-04", "2024-02-29", "2024-12-31"]
assert matches == expected, f"FAIL: {matches}"
print("LOG TEST PASSED")

# CRLF edge case
crlf = "2024-05-15 10.0.0.1\r\n2024-05-16 10.0.0.2\r\n"
m = re.findall(pattern, crlf, re.MULTILINE)
print("crlf:", m)
assert m == ["2024-05-15", "2024-05-16"], m
print("CRLF TEST PASSED")

# Performance test: 200k lines
lines = []
for i in range(100000):
    lines.append(f"2024-06-{(i%28)+1:02d} 10.0.{i%256}.{(i*7)%256} some text here {i}")
    lines.append(f"noise line {i} 192.168.{i%256}.{(i*3)%256}")
big = "\n".join(lines)
t0 = time.time()
bigm = re.findall(pattern, big, re.MULTILINE)
dt = time.time() - t0
print(f"big log: {len(bigm)} matches in {dt:.2f}s ({len(big)/1024/1024:.1f} MB)")
assert dt < 30, "too slow"
print("PERF TEST PASSED")
PY_EOF
